name: Expansion Translation: How Text Length Changes Impact
snippet: Learn how expansion translation affects text length, layout, and localization. Discover causes, language rates, and smart solutions.

name: Translation Text Expansion: How it affects Design
snippet: For most languages, it is generally safe to prepare for as much as 25%-35% expansion (or contraction if you translate from another language into English, for example). However, expansion percentages vary depending on the subject matter, writing style, and sentence or string length.

name: English to Spanish Percentage Calculator - codingace.net
snippet: Enter bilingual text or counts for percentage review. Compare English, Spanish, and mixed content shares. Export clean CSV or PDF summaries for better decisions.

name: Why Layout Matters for Translation: Text Expansion and
snippet: Layout is not separate from translation quality; it is the medium through which translation reaches the reader. Text expansion is the most visible challenge. English-to-German expansion routinely runs 20–35 percent. English-to-French and English-to-Spanish often add 15–25 percent.

name: Spanish Translation and Text Length - QuickSilver Translate
snippet: Spanish text occupies more space than English by approximately 1/5 to 1/4, or 20% (a tendency which can easily be observed if you compare translations of novels between the two languages).

name: Text Expansion and Contraction in Translation | Eriksen
snippet: Translating from English into languages such as Spanish or French can result in 20-25% expansion, while German may expand as much as 35%. On the other hand, Chinese, Korean, or Japanese will usually contract, although the percentages may fluctuate significantly.

name: Text Expansion Calculator | DTP Services Berlin
snippet: Pick your target languages and enter your source volume to see expansion per language, projected word counts, an estimated page delta and a layout-risk band, all before the layout work begins.
